panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of an infant showing classic marasmus features: loose skin folds, baggy pants sign, visible loss of subcutaneous fat and muscle wasting with prominent ribs and thin limbs. Caption and in-text explicitly attribute these findings to marasmus. The article's primary topic is TAR syndrome, but the figure is specifically captioned as showing marasmus manifestations.
panels.attribution_text: Alassri et al. Thrombocytopenia with absent radii syndrome with delayed presentation of thrombocytopenic episodes: a case report.. Annals of medicine and surgery (2012) 2023. doi:10.1097/ms9.0000000000000506. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Physical examination shows loose skin folds, baggy pants sign, visible loss of fat, and muscle which suggest a Marasmus case.
in_text_mentions: Loose skin folds, the baggy pants sign, visible loss of fat, and muscle were noticed, suggesting a Marasmus case (Fig. 1). In addition to deviation of the axis of the hand laterally, bilateral absent of radii with both thumbs was noticed.
